objective: Phase 3, registered after the experiments-v2 results and disclosed as such. Phase 2 reached 90.6% cross-validated accuracy with ViT-S/14 at 448 px, last-4-block CLS pooling and four rotation views (F2). Two observations motivate this phase: raising resolution has improved cross-validated accuracy at every step (224 to 308 to 448 px), and reducing from eight to four views lowered held-out known-material accuracy (62 to 58 of 104). Phase 3 tests whether additional reflection views and a higher resolution improve accuracy further within the same latency budget.
primary_metric: Out-of-fold accuracy from grouped, stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the development pool (train + validation splits).
adoption_rule: Rungs are evaluated in the registered order, each applying its change to the best configuration adopted so far. A rung is adopted if its encoding time fits the latency budget and its out-of-fold accuracy is higher than the current best, or equal with a lower out-of-fold log-loss. Rungs over the latency budget are evaluated and reported but cannot be adopted. Validation, test and held-out results are reported for every rung and are never used to decide adoption.
latency_rationale: Interactive screening: encoding one uploaded image (all views) must take at most 3 s on the reference laptop CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS).

baseline.title: Phase 2 selection (F2): ViT-S/14, 448 px, last-4-block CLS, 4 rotation views
baseline.hypothesis: Reference point carried over from experiments-v2.

ladder.title: Six dihedral views (four rotations and two reflections)
ladder.hypothesis: Reflections are additional valid observations of an orientation-free specimen; restoring them should recover the held-out generalisation lost when views were reduced to four, at an estimated 2.35 s encoding cost.

ladder.title: Encoder resolution 518 px with four rotation views
ladder.hypothesis: Resolution has improved accuracy at every step so far; 518 px (37 x 37 patches, the DINOv2 pretraining resolution of its final stage) resolves stomata and crystals further. Four views keep the estimated encoding cost near 2.4 s.
